summary: Independently verified the HRMS RBAC / employee-data-isolation fix. Ran the existing regression suite /app/backend/tests/test_rbac_isolation.py (43/43 pass) and authored a new complementary suite /app/backend/tests/test_rbac_body_leaks.py (19/19 pass, 62 total green) that inspects JSON RESPONSE BODIES (not just status codes) on every reported endpoint, exercises the new IDOR ownership check on PUT /late-requests|/early-out-requests|/missed-punches for a request owned by another employee (all three now return 403), samples six additional deny-by-default admin routes, deep-scans the birthday widget for DOB-year leakage, and confirms 'RBAC DENY 403' backend log lines do NOT contain the JWT token or plaintext passwords. UI regression: madhan.s renders the employee dashboard with personal-only stats (23/1/0/100%) and the sanitised birthday widget with photos+names; admin renders company-wide dashboard (Research Unit 37, Support Staff 9, Attendance 38/46). No 403 popups in either portal. Only 4xx in the network log was /api/seed which is intentionally admin-only.
critical_code_review_comments: rbac.py deny middleware is a solid deny-by-default gate; however _ALLOW_RULES relies on 'role' claim from JWT — worth adding an integrity assertion that the role in the JWT still matches the DB user on privileged operations (defence in depth).

test_rbac_isolation currently only checks that ADMIN_ONLY_PATHS return 403 without also inspecting the response body for other-employee ids. The new test_rbac_body_leaks fills that gap and should be kept in CI.
server.py is 19,739 lines — should be broken into feature modules; large files make it easy to miss a leak overlay (as noted with the earlier /api/attendance missed-punch overlay bug).
